lead: This week's list has ten publications across Biology, Computer Science, Mathematics & Statistics, Neuroscience and Physics. Biology has two papers, one on genetic effects of mountain pine beetle outbreaks on lodgepole pine and one on desiccation physiology in house crickets. Computer Science has three, covering cybersecurity, robot search and graph theory, and Physics has two papers from large international collaborations (ATLAS and nEXO). Mathematics & Statistics and Neuroscience each have one paper. No papers this week link Carleton authors across units.

items.title: Effects on Genetic Architecture From Mountain Pine Beetle Mortality in Lodgepole Pine
items.summary: The authors collected cones from lodgepole pine trees killed by mountain pine beetle and from trees that survived, grew the offspring in a common garden, and genotyped 418 of them at 14,267 loci. They found reduced genetic diversity at most sampled sites and loci that differed between offspring of survivors and of killed trees, which indicates the beetle selects on pine genotype and that regeneration from survivors may increase variation linked to reduced host quality for the beetle.

items.title: Boosting Automated Vulnerability Condition Classification Through Multi-Source Information Aggregation
items.venue: IEEE International Conference on Cloud Computing Technology and Science
items.summary: The authors built a system that classifies the preconditions and postconditions of software vulnerabilities by combining several databases, including IBM X-Force Exchange and the Red Hat CVE database, instead of relying only on the National Vulnerability Database. It improved F1 scores by 3% to 18% over single-source baselines, with gains up to 69% where the NVD had little detail, and a case study on the Free5GC 5G core showed more complete attack graphs.

items.title: Risk-Sensitive Linear-Quadratic-Gaussian Graphon Mean-Field Games
items.venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization
items.summary: The paper develops a mathematical framework for very large networks of different agents who each want to minimize a cost while accounting for their own risk sensitivity. It shows that decentralized strategies can be defined and proves they form an approximate Nash equilibrium, under stated conditions, using new error estimates suited to the exponential cost, and it includes a numerical example.

items.title: Depth-of-Anesthesia Monitoring in Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery with Open BIS Validation and Neuromorphic Feasibility
items.summary: The authors validated an open implementation of the bispectral index, a clinical measure of anesthesia depth derived from EEG, against reference data from VitalDB. They also evaluated simulated population drug response under a standard PID closed-loop controller and assessed whether the same controller could be realized in a neuromorphic framework, leaving larger-cohort validation and prospective testing for future work.

items.title: Measurements of charged-particle pseudorapidity and transverse momentum distributions in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at s N N = 5.36 TeV with the ATLAS detector
items.summary: The ATLAS collaboration measured how many charged particles are produced, and their transverse momentum, in oxygen-oxygen and neon-neon collisions at 5.36 TeV, as a function of angle and collision centrality. The results are compared with hydrodynamic calculations, so they give reference data for testing models of these collisions.

items.title: nEXO radioassay program
items.summary: The nEXO collaboration reports 300 material radioactivity assays, made with several low-background counting and mass spectrometry methods, to help select clean materials for the planned nEXO double-beta decay experiment. The compilation includes some of the tightest published limits on thorium-232 and uranium-238 content, and it can save other low-radioactivity experiments from repeating material studies.

opportunities.heading: Better attack graph inputs for 5G and cloud security assessment
opportunities.what: A deep learning method combines vulnerability descriptions from several databases to label attack preconditions and postconditions. The labels feed automated attack graphs. The team also built a labelled dataset.
opportunities.market_fit: Telecom vendors and operators securing 5G cores, and security tool vendors that build attack graphs. Ericsson Canada researches 5G network security and has worked with Zhao's group.
